issues.description: The make_y_state function's parameter list in the template does not match the signature required by the problem statement and the solution. The problem statement and the solution expect make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None (i.e., it must accept a depolarization probability p), but the template defines make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) -> None (missing the p parameter). The template's docstring even documents a p parameter, but the signature omits it. This mismatch will prevent students from writing code that matches the exercise specification and the provided tests (which call make_y_state with p), causing immediate runtime/signature errors or confusion.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the template function signature to include the depolarization parameter p: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None: . Also update the template docstring to match and ensure any calls in template/tests use the same parameter order. This aligns the template with the problem statement and the solution and prevents signature mismatches during implementation and testing.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution define make_y_state(circ, q, p) that prepares a |Y> resource state with a depolarizing noise parameter p, but the template's function signature for make_y_state is def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) -> None (no p parameter). This mismatch hides an expected parameter from students, breaks the conceptual mapping (the problem asks students to simulate noise via p), and will lead to confusion and likely failing tests when students try to follow the spec or when other template functions (e.g., teleport_s) expect a make_y_state that accepts p.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the template function signature to include the depolarization parameter p to match the problem spec and solution. For example: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None and update the docstring accordingly. Ensure any internal calls or tests use the same parameter ordering and type annotation so students can map the specification to the implementation without extra cognitive load.
